findings.name: Prologue: UTO Research Center
findings.detail: Samus is dispatched to defend a Galactic Federation facility on a planet referred to in some sources as 'Tanamaar' and in others as 'Tamaar' (spelling inconsistent across sources) against Sylux and Space Pirates. She fights the boss Aberax. A stray shot activates a mysterious Artifact, which teleports Samus (and reportedly Sylux) to the unknown planet Viewros.
findings.trackable: Story/cutscene progression, not a discrete counter.

findings.name: Main goal: Master Teleportation Keys
findings.detail: On Viewros, Samus reunites with technician Myles MacKenzie and learns she must collect 5 Master Teleportation Keys (one per major region) to activate a Master Teleporter and return home.
findings.trackable: Not confirmed whether keys have a dedicated HUD/inventory counter; likely tracked via map/inventory screen (standard for Metroid Prime items) but not verified.

findings.name: Sol Valley
findings.detail: Central desert hub region of planet Viewros that connects all major biomes. Contains Chrono Tower at its center.
findings.trackable: Region visited status likely shown on map.

findings.name: Fury Green
findings.detail: Jungle biome, west of Sol Valley. First major region explored; Samus acquires early Psychic abilities here (Psychic Visor, Psychic Glove, Missile Launcher, elemental shots: Fire, Ice, Thunder). Boss: Carvex, fought at the Garden of Remembrance.

findings.name: Volt Forge
findings.detail: Southwest region, a three-tower complex. Samus obtains the Vi-O-La Suit and Psychic Boots here. Bosses: Flight Drone MCU (mini-boss, Tower 2 Generator), Sylux (1st encounter, Tower 2 Generator), Xelios (Tower 3), and a second Sylux encounter (Tower 1 Power Core).

findings.name: Ice Belt
findings.detail: Northwest region. Samus meets companion Reger Tokabi and gains the Psychic Lasso and Psychic Boost Ball. Boss: Keratos, fought at the Quarantine Chamber.

findings.name: Flare Pool
findings.detail: Southeast (volcanic/magma) region. Samus is reunited with Federation allies Ezra Duke and Nora Armstrong, gains the Psychic Grapple. Bosses: Hover Shuttle Transport (mini-boss, Control Room Bridge), Behemoth (mini-boss, Expansion Site), and Phenoros (Volcano Heart).

findings.name: Great Mines
findings.detail: Northeast mining-base region. Combat robot companion VUE-995 joins Samus here. She obtains Super Missile and Psychic Power Bomb. Boss: Omega Griever, fought at Crystal Extraction.

findings.name: Chrono Tower
findings.detail: Central/final region within Sol Valley. Samus acquires the Legacy Suit here. Final story boss encounters occur here: Varmis (Sol Valley sand pit, tied to rebuild of a Galactic Federation mech), and the final Sylux confrontation at 'the Pinnacle'.

findings.name: Aberax
findings.detail: Fought during the Prologue at the UTO Research Center Hangar, before Samus is transported to Viewros.
findings.trackable: Likely a logbook/bestiary scan entry (three logbook scans in the Prologue are noted as missable).

findings.name: Carvex
findings.detail: Guardian-type boss ('huge, planet-like creature with multiple targets') fought at the Garden of Remembrance in Fury Green.

findings.name: Flight Drone MCU
findings.detail: Mini-boss fought at Tower 2 Generator, Volt Forge.

findings.name: Sylux (1st encounter)
findings.detail: Recurring rival/antagonist boss; first mid-game fight at Tower 2 Generator, Volt Forge, occurring immediately after the Flight Drone encounter.
findings.trackable: Presumed logbook entry; Sylux is the game's main recurring antagonist with multiple fights.

findings.name: Xelios
findings.detail: Armored machine boss encountered in the depths of Volt Forge's Tower 3.

findings.name: Keratos
findings.detail: Boulder-like boss fought at the Quarantine Chamber in Ice Belt.

findings.name: Hover Shuttle Transport
findings.detail: Mini-boss fought at the Control Room Bridge, Flare Pool.

findings.name: Behemoth
findings.detail: Mini-boss fought at the Expansion Site, Flare Pool.

findings.name: Phenoros
findings.detail: Boss fought at Volcano Heart, Flare Pool.

findings.name: Omega Griever
findings.detail: Boss fought at Crystal Extraction, Great Mines.

findings.name: Varmis
findings.detail: Boss encountered in a sand pit in the north of Sol Valley; fight triggers during the rebuild of a Galactic Federation mech.

findings.name: Sylux (2nd encounter)
findings.detail: Second Sylux fight, at Tower 1 Power Core, Volt Forge (per Game8 boss list; note this places two Sylux fights inside Volt Forge — order/placement should be re-verified before building trophy text).

findings.name: Sylux (Final Boss)
findings.detail: Final story boss fight, at 'the Pinnacle' in Chrono Tower.

findings.name: Antagonist and setting lore
findings.detail: The planet is Viewros, home to an extinct race called the Lamorn, who sought to preserve their legacy through psychic cultivation of a 'memory fruit.' Sylux is a rogue/rival bounty hunter (revealed in the secret ending to be a former Galactic Federation captain who disobeyed orders to obtain a Space Pirate weapon; the plan backfired and Samus destroyed the weapon, causing his hatred of her). The game is set between Metroid: Other M and Metroid Fusion.

findings.name: Psychic powers / Psychic Visor
findings.detail: New entry-specific mechanic: psychic abilities (distinct from the classic Scan Visor lineage) let Samus operate specialized mechanisms, see hidden platforms, and perform guided shots. Includes Psychic Visor, Psychic Glove, Psychic Boots, Psychic Lasso, Psychic Boost Ball, Psychic Grapple, and Psychic Power Bomb as named upgrades acquired through the campaign.
findings.trackable: Ability unlocks likely shown in an upgrades/inventory menu (standard Prime-series convention), not independently confirmed for this title.

findings.name: Vi-O-La motorcycle
findings.detail: A rideable motorcycle/hoverbike used as a hub-world traversal tool across Viewros. A related suit, the 'Vi-O-La Suit,' is obtained in Volt Forge.

findings.name: Bullet-time mechanic
findings.detail: Retro Studios added a bullet-time style mechanic tied to Samus's abilities (reported in pre-release press coverage); exact trigger/name not confirmed via post-release guides in this search pass.

findings.name: Normal ending
findings.detail: Samus narrowly escapes Viewros, leaving 5 Galactic Troopers (companions) behind; using remaining energy from the Master Teleporter, she is transported to another planet, hinted to be Tanamaar/Tamaar.

findings.name: Secret / 100% ending
findings.detail: Unlocked only by reaching 100% completion of both item collection AND logbook scans. Shows the same escape scene but with Samus's helmet removed (first time her face is shown in this game), plus an additional scene revealing Sylux's backstory as a former Galactic Federation captain who disobeyed orders, obtained a Space Pirate weapon, caused a disaster, and had the weapon destroyed by Samus -- explaining his hatred of her.
findings.trackable: Tied directly to the 100% item + 100% logbook completion trackers.

findings.name: Hard Mode
findings.detail: Hard Mode is present in the game, in keeping with Metroid Prime series tradition; per one wiki source it is unlocked after completing Normal Mode. Not independently confirmed via a primary/official Beyond-specific source in this search pass.
findings.trackable: Selectable from a difficulty/mode menu, presumably after clearing the campaign once.

findings.name: Fusion Mode / Fusion Suit
findings.detail: Present in prior Metroid Prime games (e.g., Prime Remastered) as an amiibo-unlocked extra-hard mode with a cosmetic Fusion Suit. Not confirmed to exist in Metroid Prime 4: Beyond specifically -- search results only returned general/legacy series pages, no Beyond-specific confirmation.
